results.accounting_satisfaction_rationale: Schema support and the role classification do not demonstrate that a concrete forward-accounting instance is populated completely and correctly for the governed source-unit inventory.
role_basis: Active Schema V2 defines forward_accounting as a collection of records keyed by source_unit_id and carrying one-or-more schema_carriers.
Active Schema V2 separately requires forward_complete=true.
The Schema-V2 design record identifies /semantic_accounting/forward_accounting as the dedicated forward-accounting carrier.
The requirement therefore governs the cross-cutting forward accounting relation and its completeness rather than asserting a semantic property of one particular semantic unit.
results.semantic_encoding_nonclaim: Even complete forward accounting would not by itself prove that every bound carrier preserves the source semantic losslessly.

results.accounting_satisfaction_rationale: Schema support and the role classification do not demonstrate that a concrete reverse-accounting instance is populated completely and correctly for all governed schema carriers and source-unit relations.
role_basis: Active Schema V2 defines reverse_accounting as a collection of records keyed by schema_carrier and carrying one-or-more source_unit_ids.
Active Schema V2 separately requires reverse_complete=true.
The Schema-V2 design record identifies /semantic_accounting/reverse_accounting as the dedicated reverse-accounting carrier.
The requirement therefore governs the cross-cutting reverse accounting relation and its completeness rather than asserting a semantic property of one particular semantic unit.
results.semantic_encoding_nonclaim: Even complete reverse accounting would not by itself prove deterministic exact reconstruction of every source semantic.
